BeforeCombatStartLate.issue: Rollup of guards G1, G2 and G3 per binding rule 4. The relic's own logic -- procure one Potion Shaped Rock at the start of every combat -- is ported and the potion exists, but the port reaches the belt through PlayerCombatState.add_potion instead of the game's PotionCmd.TryToProcure, which drops the two hooks that verb exists to run (G1, G2), and it lands in the sim's single on_combat_start pass instead of the source's LATE phase (G3).

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the procure skips `Hook.ShouldProcurePotion`, so Sozu does not refuse the rock
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PotionCmd.TryToProcure (src/Core/Commands/PotionCmd.cs:28-39) opens with `if (!Hook.ShouldProcurePotion(...)) return NotAllowed;` before it ever calls Player.AddPotionInternal, and PetrifiedToad.cs:19 goes through TryToProcure. petrified_toad.py:20 calls PlayerCombatState.add_potion, whose own docstring states the omission outright: 'Combat-side procurement (Alchemize, Delicate Frond, Petrified Toad) does not run the Hook.ShouldProcurePotion gate today ... out of scope' (player.py:112-115). The run-side twin DOES run it (RunState.add_potion, run.py:479-481). REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-toad): Sozu is ported and returns False from should_procure_potion (relics/sozu.py:26-27) and is granted by the ported Darv shrine; with both relics attached the sim's belt still reads ['PotionShapedRock', None, None] where the game leaves it empty. Both relics are ported, obtainable and can be held together, and the code path is taken on the first turn of every combat, so nothing further is needed. FILED AS A GAP, NOT WAIVED under the contract's potion exclusion, because the divergence is a dropped HOOK DISPATCH rather than potion bookkeeping: the same missing gate applies to every combat-side procure the sim has, and the potion is only the payload. NOTE per binding rule 7: PotionCmd.cs, player.py, run.py and relics/sozu.py are NOT hashed by this record.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the procure skips `Hook.AfterPotionProcured`, so Belt Buckle keeps its 2 Dexterity when the Toad's rock lands
guards.issue: MECHANISM: PotionCmd.TryToProcure fires `await Hook.AfterPotionProcured(...)` on success (PotionCmd.cs:46). Belt Buckle implements it and REMOVES the 2 Dexterity the moment the belt stops being empty; audit/records/relic/belt_buckle.json already verdicts that missing sim counterpart a LIVE gap at Belt Buckle's own site, so this entry matches that verdict per binding rule 3 and records the TRIGGER half rather than re-deriving the mechanism. What this record adds is that Petrified Toad is a second ported trigger for it, and one that fires unconditionally at the start of every single combat rather than only when the player chooses to pick a potion up. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- b12-toad): with [belt_buckle, petrified_toad] the sim opens combat at Dexterity 2 with one potion held, where the game opens at Dexterity 0 with one potion held. Both relics are ported and in the transcribed grab bag (Shop and Uncommon). NOTE per binding rule 7: PotionCmd.cs and belt_buckle.json are not hashed here.

guards.what: G3 (LIVE): the hook is BeforeCombatStart**Late** and the sim has no phase concept, so the outcome of the Belt Buckle interaction depends on relic pickup ORDER where the game's is fixed
guards.rationale: FIXED 2026-07-28. `PetrifiedToad.on_combat_start` was renamed to `on_combat_start_late` (sts2_rl/relics/petrified_toad.py), the pass PetrifiedToad.cs:16's `BeforeCombatStartLate` belongs to. `HookSystem.on_combat_start` dispatches through `_each`'s phase walk, so the rock is procured after every plain-pass combat-start listener -- which is what puts it behind Belt Buckle's belt-widening whatever order the two relics were acquired in. The recorded witness (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b12.py b12-toad`, which returned two different combat-start states from the same two relics depending on order) no longer diverges. The relic's own docstring already named the C# hook correctly.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: MECHANISM: Hook.BeforeCombatStart (src/Core/Hooks/Hook.cs:311-323) runs a COMPLETE listener pass calling BeforeCombatStart, then a second complete pass calling BeforeCombatStartLate. Petrified Toad is the ONLY BeforeCombatStartLate implementer in the whole decompiled game (`grep -rln 'override.*BeforeCombatStartLate' src/` returns src/Core/Models/Relics/PetrifiedToad.cs alone), and it uses the Late phase to guarantee the procure happens after every plain combat-start effect -- notably after Belt Buckle has applied its Dexterity, which is what makes the removal in G2 deterministic. The sim collapses both phases onto on_combat_start, a single walk in relic-registration order. EXECUTED (b12-toad): [belt_buckle, petrified_toad] leaves Dexterity 2, and [petrified_toad, belt_buckle] leaves Dexterity None -- the sim produces two different combat-start states from the same two relics depending on which was picked up first, where the game produces one (1 potion, 0 Dexterity) either way. This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G3 (missing Early/VeryEarly/Late phase passes, 24 of Hook.cs's 147 dispatchers) at a new site; that record labels the mechanism LIVE and one verdict per mechanism applies (binding rule 3), so this entry matches it and contributes the observable. NOTE per binding rule 7: Hook.cs, PetrifiedToad.cs is hashed but hook_dispatch.json and belt_buckle.py are not.

guards.what: N1: the potion itself -- `PotionCmd.TryToProcure<PotionShapedRock>` (PetrifiedToad.cs:19) vs `PotionShapedRock()` (petrified_toad.py:19-20) -- and the belt-full failure mode
guards.rationale: The potion is ported (sts2_rl/potions.py defines PotionShapedRock) and the silent-failure semantics match: Player.AddPotionInternal takes `slotIndex = _potionSlots.IndexOf(null)` and fails when the belt is full, and PlayerCombatState.add_potion (player.py:107-121) mirrors it exactly -- `if None not in self.potions: return False`, then fill the first null slot, never compacting. Slot IDENTITY is load-bearing in this codebase (a UsePotion replay command names a slot), and both sides pick the first free slot rather than appending, so a Toad rock does not shift an existing potion's slot. Combat-procured potions do reach the run: RunState.finish_combat copies `self.potions = list(combat.player.potions)` (run.py:1182), so the rock survives the fight exactly as the game's does. Verified by execution rather than asserted (b12-toad prints the belt). NOTE per binding rule 7: potions.py, player.py and run.py are not hashed here.
